wacc.formula: WACC = wₑ × kₑ + w_d × k_d × (1 − t);  kₑ = r_f + β × ERP
steps: β (Blume-adjusted) = 0.67 × raw β 0.20 + 0.33 = 0.46  (104 weekly returns vs SPY, R² 0.01)
k_d = 7.10%  (10-year Treasury + 2% (no rate on file)); after tax 7.10% × (1 − 21%) = 5.61%

methods.formula: Value per share = (peer median EV/Sales × Revenue − net debt) ÷ shares
methods.fit: It has revenue ($201.2B over four quarters), and 37 peers (SIC 1311) have the multiple.

methods.formula: Value per share = weighted peer median EV/Sales × Revenue (− net debt, ÷ shares); weight of a peer's multiple = size weight × recency weight
steps: 37 peers, 579 observations (today and every quarter since 2022); the weights amount to 9.1 equal peers
medians: every peer alike, today only (the plain median) 2.4x; by market value 2.1x; by revenue 2.1x; by recency only (quarters since 2022, half-life one year) 2.8x; all together 2.1x
inputs: shares of the peers' market value, revenue and trading value
assumptions: geometric mean of the peer's shares of market value, revenue and trading value
an assumption: the largest peer weighs most but is never the whole answer
an assumption: last year's quarters count half
median daily close × volume, last 63 sessions
methods.fit: It has revenue ($201.2B over four quarters), and 37 peers (SIC 1311) have the multiple. Weighting the peers by market value, revenue and trading value, and their quarters by recency, keeps small, thinly traded peers and old prices from moving the multiple as much.
